title: Ordered Dequant Bypass, SmoothStat Collector, and KV-Consistent Routing for Quant Kernels
author: Aisha Patel
description:
Motivation: We observed tail latency spikes and extra memory traffic when serving mixed-precision (INT8/FP8) workloads with prefix reuse. Root causes: (1) unnecessary materialization/dequant roundtrips for attention weight paths that are not used by the current request ordering, (2) imprecise per-head statistics collection for SmoothQuant that caused kernel divergence at scale, and (3) inconsistent KV routing when dequant fusion changes node layouts, which invalidates batching alignment heuristics.

This PR introduces an ordered dequant-bypass path that avoids dequantization and re-quantization for heads/blocks that are not referenced by the active request ordering, a SmoothStatCollector that computes activation scaling stats deterministically across batching boundaries, and a lightweight KV-consistent routing layer that pins fused-kernel variants to routing keys so continuous batching remains compatible with fusion-driven layout changes.

Summary of changes (single-line items):
- Add OrderedDequantBypass planner and runtime hooks to skip dequant on non-referenced heads.
- Implement SmoothStatCollector which aggregates per-channel activation scales using deterministic reduce ops and exposes stats to kernel selection.
- Introduce KVRoutingFingerprint to bind fused dequant kernels to routing keys used by the continuous batching router.
- Kernel change: fused_dequant_matmul_{int8,fp8}.cu updated to accept bypass flags and stat references.
- Runtime scheduler: update batching compatibility checks to consult KVRoutingFingerprint and ordered bypass masks.
- Add unit/integration tests and a perf microbenchmark harness.

Checklist: 
- [x] Design doc linked in Linear ENG-4821
- [x] Unit tests for planner and collector
- [x] Perf harness and baseline regression tests
- [x] Backwards-compatible: falls back to existing dequant path when feature flag off
- [x] QA on Dedicated staging with mixed small/large sequence workloads

Performance impact (end-to-end on our internal bert-like inference with 1-128 seq batch mix):
- 1.18x throughput increase on INT8 end-to-end path (p99 latency unchanged or improved)
- 12% average per-request memory traffic reduction in KV store windows due to bypassed materialization
- 7-9% lower latency tail in small-rt workloads (1-16 seq) when SmoothStatCollector is enabled
- Demonstrated no perf regression on FP8 float-ref path

Testing and CI: initial CI run had two flaky tests (perf/regression) failing on the runner; those were addressed by re-seeding the test harness and adding a small timing tolerance in test_assert_harness. Final CI: all checks pass (unit/integration/perf/e2e).

Backward compatibility and rollout plan: feature gated behind runtime flag `quant.ordered_dequant_bypass` and SmoothStatCollector behind `quant.smooth_stat_collect`. We will rollout as a staged canary: 5% -> 25% -> 100% on Dedicated clusters, with automated regression gates tied to the perf harness.

Related Linear/Jira: ENG-4821, ENG-4890; customer incident SUP-2219 triggered additional KV routing constraints.

Notes on implementation details: OrderedDequantBypass computes a per-request bitmask of referenced heads/blocks at pre-schedule time and attaches a compact 64-bit mask to the continuous-batch entry. The fused kernel accepts the mask and only materializes dequantized weights for set bits; non-materialized blocks are read via a fast-path that treats weights as quantized during matmul with calibrated scaling. SmoothStatCollector runs as a prewarm operator in the batch window that reduces activation max/mean stats with deterministic tree reduction to avoid non-determinism across batching orders. KVRoutingFingerprint derives a stable 128-bit fingerprint from the fused-kernel signature and the model's routing key; the router pins kernel variants to fingerprinted slots so existing batch aggregator assumptions remain valid.

review_comments: Kunal Mehta (review): Nice work. Two questions: can we bound the worst-case CPU overhead of the SmoothStatCollector on tiny batches? Also please document the seed behavior in test harness so future flakes are easier to triage.

Aisha Patel (author): SmoothStatCollector runs on the batch leader only and uses SIMD-friendly reductions; measured CPU overhead < 2% in our microbench. Added comment + test that seeds the harness (see commit f12b3d0).
Liam O'Connor (review): I saw a small runtime issue when routing pinned kernel variants across regions due to signer differences. Can we ensure fingerprint generation is region-agnostic?

Aisha Patel (author): KVRoutingFingerprint uses model+kernel signature + normalized routing key; removed non-deterministic signer data. Added stable serialization step to ensure region-agnostic fingerprints.
Sofia Martinez (approval): Verified perf harness results; approve.
release_notes: Added Ordered Dequant Bypass to reduce unnecessary dequantization for non-referenced heads, introduced SmoothStatCollector for deterministic SmoothQuant stats across batching boundaries, and added KVRoutingFingerprint to maintain batching compatibility with fused dequant kernels. Performance improvements for INT8 paths and reduced KV memory traffic. Feature gated and rolled out via canary.
notes: This PR aims to be non-breaking: default flags are off until canary completes.
Follow-up tasks: ENG-4951 add metric for bypass hit-rate, ENG-4972 expand kernel unit coverage for exotic model layouts.
Bench harness and datasets used are checked into perf/benchmarks and are deterministic when run with --seed flag.
